reason: Prior evidence favors testing the approved Strassen path first: its 256-square primitive passed checks, but the complete wrapper is unmeasured and carries accuracy and data-movement risks. The next two proposals use nearly the same Strassen schedule, so their results may not isolate individual choices. Panel packing and fused transpose have plausible locality benefits, but are unmeasured; prior panel and traversal variants did not promote. Tile remapping and FMOPA scheduling have low expected upside given prior non-promotions. Tail alignment and the C fallback do not target the fixed n=512 path. Assembly audit ranks last because legal post-index loads for the required unequal strides are unverified, and prior evidence says the proposed form is unavailable.
